module: D10-13 Trade Policy／Export Controls／Sanctions Supply-chain Transmission貿易政策出口管制制裁供應鏈傳導
purpose: Establish issuer-level, effective-dated Taiwan semiconductor export-control exposure using current official rule text plus issuer-native product/location/compliance evidence.

policyVintages.evidence: Additional due-diligence measures for advanced-computing ICs broadened foundry/packaging licensing and reporting obligations, with approved/authorized designer and approved OSAT pathways.
The January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule had a May 15 compliance date but was rescinded before enforcement; this is a policy-lifecycle negative control.
BIS revised licensing policy for H200/MI325X-class chips and similar products to case-by-case review under specified security conditions.
Timeline for certain authorized IC designer treatment extended through 2026-12-31.

ruleState.advancedNodeDefinition: Logic non-planar transistor architecture at 16/14nm or less is included in the advanced-node definition; memory thresholds are separately defined.
ruleState.endUseControl: EAR 744.23 imposes licensing restrictions for specified supercomputer, advanced-node IC and semiconductor-manufacturing end uses/end users.
ruleState.approvedDesignerAndOsatMechanism: EAR Part 740 supplements identify approved IC designers and approved OSAT companies; approval status can be revised, suspended or revoked.
ruleState.taiwanCountryContext: Taiwan appears in the AI Authorization Countries supplement, but country status does not remove transaction/product/end-use/end-user duties.

issuerExposure.productScope: Foundry spanning advanced and mature nodes; 2025 wafer revenue includes 3nm/5nm/7nm/16nm and older nodes.
issuerNativePolicyEvidence: 2025 Form 20-F states January 2025 rules may require export licenses before shipping products using 16nm or below process to specified destinations unless conditions are met.
TSMC Nanjing's prior VEU authorization expired in December 2025; U.S. Commerce granted an annual export license allowing U.S.-controlled items to continue being supplied to the Nanjing fab.
TSMC states current operations had not been materially affected by expanded export-control regulations as of the annual-report date, while future risk remains.
TSMC export management uses 'No ECCN, No Shipment' and requires customer end-use and ECCN information for applicable licensing.

issuerExposure.officialPolicyRole: Listed by BIS as an Approved Integrated Circuit Designer in Part 740 supplement 6.
issuerExposure.note: Approved status changes compliance treatment but is not a blanket exemption from all export controls.

issuerExposure.officialPolicyRole: Listed by BIS as an Approved Integrated Circuit Designer in Part 740 supplement 6.
Listed by BIS as an Approved OSAT company in Part 740 supplement 7.
issuerExposure.companyScope: Global foundry focused on logic and specialty technologies with most core fabs/R&D in Taiwan and additional Asian fabs.
issuerExposure.note: Approved listing is a compliance-pathway fact, not proof of low business impact.

negativeControls: AI Diffusion Rule was formally issued with a future compliance date and then rescinded before that date; publication alone cannot be treated as realized supply-chain exposure.

Taiwan country authorization status and approved designer/OSAT listing can reduce or reshape compliance burden for some transactions; export-control impact is not one-directional across Taiwan issuers.
TSMC disclosed an annual license preserving Nanjing supply continuity after VEU expiry; a rule tightening does not mechanically imply fab shutdown.
TSMC also disclosed no material current operational impact as of its 2025 report date, despite direct exposure to tighter rules; policy relevance != realized earnings damage.

pitContract.amendmentRule: Rule amendments, rescissions, list-status changes and license renewals append new vintages; never rewrite prior states.
pitContract.outcomeFirewall: No stock, revenue, margin or market-share outcome is opened while freezing the exposure state.

redundancyControls: D11/D17 own event/news timing; D10-13 owns physical/economic supply-chain exposure.
D13-17 owns broad macro/geopolitical financial-condition transmission.
D10-08 shortage is a possible downstream state, not a duplicate policy vote.
Approved-list status, annual licenses and country classification modify exposure uncertainty; they do not create separate Alpha votes.
promotionReason: Current BIS rule text plus issuer-native TSMC location/process/compliance/license disclosures and approved Taiwan designer/OSAT lists form an effective-dated, replayable issuer exposure dataset with explicit negative controls and UNKNOWN handling.
reasonNoL4: No prospective/OOS evidence links these policy-exposure states to future issuer revenue, margin, market share or stock-selection utility after controlling for product mix, customer geography, market regime and event effects.
exactNext: SC-047 append future BIS rule/list/license changes prospectively and maintain issuer exposure vintages without backfill.
Add issuer-native customer/destination revenue exposure only where disclosed on compatible denominators; otherwise keep magnitude UNKNOWN.
Preregister prospective outcome windows before testing revenue/margin/stock effects.
